All other processed food, such as biscuits, ice cream, jam, kimchi, milk, mooncakes, nuts and wine, from any country: a combined weight of no more than 5 kg or 5 litres and a total value not exceeding $100 per traveller. Cleaned dried bird's nest is limited to 1 kg with no value limit.
Can I bring meat into Singapore?
Only from the approved countries the SFA lists for each type. Beef is limited to 5 kg; the table gives no weight limit for mutton, pork and poultry, but they must come from approved countries.
Can I bring eggs into Singapore?

Up to 30 chicken shell eggs from approved countries such as Australia, Japan, Malaysia (West), the USA, Thailand and others. Egg products not listed, such as free-range and processed eggs, are not allowed.
Can I bring fruit and vegetables into Singapore?
Yes, from any country, in a small, reasonable (hand-carry size) quantity for private consumption. The SFA gives no numeric limit.

topics.label: Meat
topics.head: Meat is allowed only from approved countries; beef is limited to 5 kg.

lines: Beef: 5 kg, from countries such as Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Spain, the UK, USA and others on the SFA list.
Mutton, pork and poultry: no weight limit is stated in the table, but each has its own approved-country list. The page says meat includes all food products containing meat.

topics.label: Fish & seafood
topics.head: Fish products from all countries; some shellfish are limited or banned.

lines: Fish products (live fish, fillets, canned tuna, dried fish) from all countries, with no limit stated.
Frozen cooked crabmeat and prawn meat from all countries: 5 kg in total, of which no more than 2 kg crabmeat and prawn meat. Live or frozen oysters only from approved countries.
Chilled shucked raw oysters and chilled crabmeat are not allowed from any source.

topics.label: Eggs
topics.head: Up to 30 chicken shell eggs from approved countries.

lines: 30 chicken shell eggs, from approved countries including Australia, Brunei, Denmark, Finland, Indonesia, Ireland, Japan, Malaysia (West), the Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, Spain, Sweden, Korea, Thailand, Ukraine, Turkiye and the USA.
Egg products that are not listed, such as free-range and processed eggs, are not allowed.

topics.label: Fruit & veg
topics.head: Fruit and vegetables from any country in a small hand-carry quantity.

lines: From all countries and regions, a small, reasonable quantity, meaning hand-carry size, for private consumption. No numeric limit is given.

topics.label: Processed food
topics.head: Processed food: 5 kg or 5 litres and $100 in total per traveller.

scen.when: Biscuits, milk, nuts, wine and more
lines: Combined weight no more than 5 kg or 5 litres, and total value no more than $100 per traveller.
The page has no separate dairy category: milk counts as processed food. Cleaned dried bird’s nest: 1 kg with no value limit.
The SFA says the current rules continue to apply while the Food Safety and Security Act is phased in; its page dates are inconsistent, so check the live page before you travel.

United Arab Emirates.answer: Dubai Customs' Passenger Customs Guide lists food products among the goods accompanying passengers that are subject to permits from the relevant authorities, and says food items may not be brought in by a traveller in commercial quantity under the names of individuals. Baggage and gifts must be of a personal nature and not in commercial quantities. The guide's list of items not allowed includes betel leaves (paan) and nasvaar, and it does not give a list of permitted or banned foods.
sources: https://www.dubaicustoms.gov.ae/en/OpenData/Publications/PassengerCustomsGuide.pdf
Dubai Customs — Passenger Customs Guide (version 6, 2025)
faq: Do I need a permit to bring food into the UAE?

Dubai Customs lists food products among the goods accompanying passengers that are subject to permits by the relevant authorities. The guide does not say which foods or amounts need one; Dubai Municipality is named as a strategic partner.
Can I bring a lot of food as a traveller?

No. The guide says food items are not allowed to be brought in by a traveller in commercial quantity under the names of individuals, and baggage must be of a personal nature and not in commercial quantities.
Are agricultural seedlings with soil allowed?
No. The guide says agricultural seedlings containing soil are not allowed to be brought in by a traveller; plants and seedlings are also on its permit list.
Which items does Dubai Customs say are not allowed?
Examples include narcotics, indecent materials, gambling machines, counterfeit goods and money, and nasvaar and betel leaves (paan) of any kind.

topics.label: Food products
topics.head: Food is on the list of goods subject to permits from the relevant authorities.

lines: The guide lists food products among goods accompanying passengers that are subject to permits by the relevant authorities. It does not say which foods or amounts.
Check with the authority before you bring any food, especially meat, dairy or fresh produce; we did not find a list of permitted foods.

topics.label: Commercial quantities
topics.head: Food in commercial quantity cannot be brought in under an individual’s name.

lines: Food items are not allowed to be brought in by a traveller in commercial quantity under the names of individuals.
Baggage and gifts must be of a personal nature and not in commercial quantities, and the passenger must not be someone who trades in them.

topics.label: Plants & seedlings
topics.head: Seedlings with soil are not allowed; plants need a permit.

lines: Agricultural seedlings containing soil are not allowed to be brought in by a traveller.
Plants and seedlings are listed among the goods that are subject to permits by the relevant authorities.

topics.label: Items not allowed
topics.head: Betel leaves (paan) and nasvaar of any kind are banned.

lines: Nasvaar and betel leaves (paan) of any kind, narcotics, indecent and obscene materials, gambling tools and machines, counterfeit goods and counterfeit money.
Also any other goods the importation of which is banned under UAE laws or the GCC Common Customs Law.
The guide does not list permitted or banned foods, penalties for food, or the rules of Dubai Municipality; ask the authority before you travel with food.

Philippines.answer: The Philippines regulates plants and plant products through the Bureau of Plant Industry (BPI). For personal use you need a Plant Quarantine Clearance (PQC) from BPI before you travel, plus a phytosanitary certificate from the country you travel from, and you must declare the product and show both documents at the airport; without them it may be confiscated. A product that is not on BPI's list of allowed commodities may not be brought in. The BPI advisory we read is written for travellers from Thailand and mentions a limit of 10 kg for personal consumption.
sources: https://npqsd.bpi-npqsd.com.ph/2026/04/27/advisory-for-travelers-bringing-agricultural-products-into-the-philippines-for-personal-consumption-ref-no-advisory-bkpe-01-2025/
BPI National Plant Quarantine Services Division — Advisory for travelers: bringing agricultural products into the Philippines for personal consumption (27 April 2026)
https://npqsd.bpi-npqsd.com.ph/import/
BPI National Plant Quarantine Services Division — Import (Plant Quarantine Clearance and allowed lists)
faq: Can I bring fruit and vegetables into the Philippines?

Only if the product is on BPI's list of allowed commodities and you hold a Plant Quarantine Clearance from BPI and a phytosanitary certificate from the country you travel from. The BPI advisory we read is for travellers from Thailand and says personal consumption should not exceed 10 kg.
What documents do I need to bring plants or planting materials?

A Plant Quarantine Clearance (PQC) issued by the Bureau of Plant Industry and a phytosanitary certificate issued by the plant authority of the country you travel from. On arrival you declare the product and present both documents to Customs and Plant Quarantine officers at the airport.
What happens if I arrive without the clearance?
The advisory says the products may be confiscated by the authorities at the airport.
Where do I check whether a product is allowed?
BPI publishes a downloadable list of allowable plants and planting materials (the version we read is dated 15 October 2026) and a separate list of allowable fruits and vegetables on its import page.

topics.label: Fresh fruit & vegetables
topics.head: Fruit and vegetables need a BPI clearance and a certificate from the exporting country.

scen.when: Fruit, vegetables, ornamental plants or planting materials
lines: Check BPI's list of allowed commodities first: a product that is not on the list may not be brought in.
You need a Plant Quarantine Clearance (PQC) from BPI and a phytosanitary certificate from the plant authority of the country you travel from, both obtained before you travel.
Declare the product on arrival and present the PQC and the certificate to Customs and Plant Quarantine officers at the airport.
The BPI advisory we read is written for travellers coming from Thailand and states that personal consumption should not exceed 10 kg.
It does not say whether the same limit applies to other departure countries.

topics.label: Plants & seeds
topics.head: Plants and planting materials follow the same clearance and allowed-list rules.

lines: BPI says anyone importing plants or plant products applies for a PQC before importing; a PQC is for personal use, while commercial imports use a different clearance.
The BPI import page says an application for a PQC is filed in person at the NPQSD central office, so ask BPI how this works for a traveller before you fly.
BPI's list of allowable plants and planting materials is a downloadable spreadsheet that it calls a living document, updated regularly.

topics.label: If you have no clearance
topics.head: Without the PQC and the certificate, officers may confiscate the products at the airport.

lines: The advisory says that if you do not obtain both the PQC and the phytosanitary certificate before you arrive, the products may be confiscated at the airport.

topics.head: We did not read the rules for meat, dairy, eggs or packaged food.

lines: The pages we read cover plants and plant products only; they say nothing about meat, dairy, eggs or packaged food.
Declare any food on arrival and ask the Department of Agriculture before you bring meat, dairy, eggs or packaged food.

India.answer: Indian Customs asks every arriving passenger to say whether they carry meat, dairy, fish or poultry products, and whether they carry seeds, plants, fruits, flowers or other planting material. Anyone who answers yes goes to the Red Channel. Plants and their produce, such as fruits and seeds, are listed as restricted goods, so they are allowed only under conditions. Non-declaration or concealment is an offence that can lead to confiscation, fines and prosecution. The pages we read give no quantity limits for food.
sources: https://www.cbic.gov.in/resources/htdocs-cbec/travellerguide_atithi.pdf
CBIC (Indian Customs) — Guide for International Travellers (PDF)
https://www.cbic.gov.in/resources/htdocs-cbec/customs_clearance_of_passengers_at_a_glance.pdf
CBIC (Indian Customs) — Customs Clearance of Passengers at a Glance (PDF)
faq: Do I have to declare food when I arrive in India?

The Customs baggage declaration form asks whether you are bringing meat and meat products, dairy, fish or poultry products, and whether you are bringing seeds, plants, fruits, flowers or other planting material. If you answer yes to these items you report to the Red Channel.
Can I bring fruit, seeds or plants into India?

Indian Customs lists plants and their produce, such as fruits and seeds, as restricted goods: they can be brought in only under conditions. The pages we read do not state those conditions, so ask Indian customs or the nearest Indian mission before you bring any.
What is the Red Channel and the Green Channel?

Passengers with nothing dutiable or prohibited may use the Green Channel. Passengers who need to declare goods, or who carry items from the declaration form such as meat, dairy, plants or seeds, must use the Red Channel.
What happens if I do not declare?
Non-declaration, mis-declaration or concealment is an offence under the Customs Act, 1962. It can lead to confiscation of the goods, fines and penalties, and prosecution.

The Customs leaflet lists plants and their produce, such as fruits and seeds, as restricted goods, meaning goods allowed only under certain conditions.
The leaflet does not name the conditions, a permit or a quantity.

lines: Passengers who need to declare goods for duty, or who carry items subject to import prohibitions listed in the declaration form, must report to the Red Channel.
Walking through the Green Channel with prohibited, restricted or dutiable goods can lead to penal action.

topics.label: If you do not declare
topics.head: Non-declaration or concealment can mean confiscation, fines and prosecution.

lines: The guide says non-declaration, mis-declaration or concealment is an offence under the Customs Act, 1962.
Depending on how serious it is, goods can be confiscated outright or released after a redemption fine, penalties can be imposed, and the passenger can be arrested and prosecuted.

topics.head: We did not read India's plant and animal quarantine rules.

lines: The Customs pages we read give no weight limit and no list of allowed foods. We did not read India's plant and animal quarantine rules: the Plant Quarantine site could not be opened when we checked.
Ask Indian customs or the nearest Indian mission before you bring meat, dairy, fruit, seeds or plants.

Indonesia.answer: Indonesia's quarantine agency Badan Karantina asks travellers returning from abroad to declare their baggage in the All Indonesia app, and passengers carrying commodities that need quarantine inspection must report them and have them checked by quarantine officers at the airport. Bringing animals, fish, plants or their products without quarantine documents from the place of origin is a violation. The agency also bans commodities at risk of Nipah virus from countries not free of it, including Malaysia, and seizes and destroys them. The page we read gives no quantity limits.
sources: https://karantinaindonesia.go.id/berita/pengawasan-produk-hewan-dan-tumbuhan-asal-luar-negeri-terus-diperketat
Badan Karantina Indonesia — Oversight of animal and plant products from abroad is tightened (6 April 2026)
faq: Do I have to declare food or plants when I arrive in Indonesia?

Badan Karantina asks travellers to declare their baggage in the All Indonesia app, and passengers carrying commodities that require quarantine inspection must report them and have them checked by quarantine officers at the airport.
Can I bring meat, fruit or vegetables into Indonesia?

The agency's oversight focuses on meat and processed meat, plants, fruit and vegetables in passenger baggage. Bringing animals, fish, plants or their products without quarantine documents from the place of origin is a violation.
Can I bring food from Malaysia?

Badan Karantina bans commodities at risk of Nipah virus contamination from countries not yet free of it, including Malaysia. If officers find them in the baggage of a passenger from Malaysia they seize and destroy them.
Are there quantity limits?
The page we read states none.

topics.label: Declare in the app
topics.head: Declare your baggage in the All Indonesia app and report quarantine commodities at the airport.

lines: Travellers returning from abroad are asked to declare their baggage in the All Indonesia app.
Passengers carrying commodities that need quarantine inspection must report them and have quarantine officers check them when they arrive at the airport.

topics.label: Meat, plants & produce
topics.head: Animals, fish, plants and their products need quarantine documents from where they come from.

scen.when: Meat, processed meat, plants, fruit and vegetables
lines: These are the items the quarantine office says it checks in passenger baggage and cargo.
Bringing animals, fish, plants or their products without quarantine documents from the area or country of origin is a violation and can lead to action under the rules.

topics.label: From Malaysia
topics.head: Commodities at risk of Nipah virus from Malaysia are banned.

lines: The quarantine agency bans commodities at risk of Nipah virus contamination from countries not yet free of the virus, including Malaysia.
If officers find them in a passenger's baggage they seize and destroy them.

topics.label: Not covered
topics.head: The page lists no quantity limits and no list of allowed foods.

lines: We read one official news page from Badan Karantina. It gives no quantity limit, no list of allowed foods, and no fine amounts.
Ask the quarantine office or check the All Indonesia app before you bring meat, dairy, eggs, plants or fruit.

Dominican Republic.answer: The Dominican customs authority (DGA) says food must be declared on the electronic e-Ticket form, and that plants, farm products, food and medicines are subject to rules of the Ministry of Agriculture or the Ministry of Public Health. Animal products fall under the Ministry of Agriculture. The traveller manual page gives no specific rules for fruit and no quantity limits for food.
sources: https://www.aduanas.gob.do/manual-del-viajero/
Dirección General de Aduanas (DGA) — Manual del Viajero
faq: Do I have to declare food when I arrive in the Dominican Republic?
Yes. The DGA traveller manual says food must be declared on the corresponding form, the electronic e-Ticket.
Who sets the rules for food, plants and animal products?

The manual says plants, farm products, food and medicines are subject to regulation by the Ministry of Agriculture or the Ministry of Public Health. Animal products are subject to the Ministry of Agriculture.
Can I bring fruit into the Dominican Republic?
The manual page contains no specific rule for fruit. Declare it and ask the Ministry of Agriculture.
Can I bring my medicines?
Medicines for personal use are allowed. Controlled or psychotropic substances need a medical prescription that justifies their use during your stay.

topics.label: Any food
topics.head: Food must be declared on the electronic e-Ticket form.

lines: The DGA manual says food must be declared on the corresponding form, the e-Ticket.
Health, plant-health and animal-health authorities regulate these products as applicable.

Poland.answer: Poland's veterinary inspectorate (GIW) says animal-origin food brought from non-EU countries for personal use is tightly limited because of disease risk: meat, milk and dairy are not allowed under the personal-use exemption, infant formula, special medical food and medically needed pet food are allowed up to 2 kg in total, gutted fish up to 20 kg, and honey, live oysters, live mussels and snails up to 2 kg. Anything that does not meet the conditions must be handed over on arrival for official disposal, and failing to declare it can mean a fine or criminal proceedings.
sources: https://www.wetgiw.gov.pl/handel-eksport-import/przywoz-zywnosci-na-wlasny-uzytek
Główny Inspektorat Weterynarii (GIW) — Bringing food and pet food for personal use
faq: Can I bring meat or dairy into Poland from a non-EU country?

Not under the personal-use exemption: meat, milk and their products are allowed only from the Faroe Islands or Greenland, up to 10 kg per person. Anything else must be handed over for official disposal.
How much fish can I bring?
From non-EU countries other than the Faroe Islands and Greenland: up to 20 kg per person, or one fish if it weighs 20 kg or more. Fresh fish must be gutted.
What can I bring for a baby or for medical reasons?

Infant formula and other infant food, special medical food and pet food needed for a pet's health: up to 2 kg in total, if it needs no refrigeration before opening, is in commercial packaging and is sealed unless already in use.
What happens if I do not declare these products?
The GIW page says failing to declare them may result in a fine or criminal proceedings.

Hungary.answer: Nébih, Hungary's food chain safety office, says meat and dairy products from non-EU countries may not be brought into the EU, including Hungary, whatever the quantity, and are confiscated. Pork and pork products are also barred from any third country or EU area hit by African swine fever. Small personal quantities of a few other animal products are allowed within weight limits, such as up to 2 kg of infant formula and honey, and up to 20 kg of gutted fish. The Nébih article we read is dated 24 January 2020.
sources: https://portal.nebih.gov.hu/-/szigoru-szabalyozas-a-poggyaszban-behozott-elelmiszerekre-vonatkozoan
Nébih — Strict rules for food brought in luggage (24 January 2020)
faq: Can I bring meat or dairy into Hungary from a non-EU country?

No. Nébih says importing meat and dairy products from third countries into the EU is prohibited regardless of quantity, so even small amounts are confiscated. The exception is up to 10 kg of meat, milk and dairy from the Faroe Islands or Greenland.
Can I bring pork?
Pork and pork products cannot be brought in from any third country or EU area where African swine fever occurs; Nébih names the Danube Delta and Szatmár county as examples.
Which small animal products are allowed?

Infant formula, baby food, special medical food and medically needed pet food: up to 2 kg in total (10 kg from the Faroe Islands or Greenland), sealed and needing no refrigeration. Honey, live oysters, mussels and snails: up to 2 kg. Gutted fish: up to 20 kg or one fish.
What happens at the border?
Products that do not meet the rules must be handed over for official destruction, and failing to declare them can lead to a fine or criminal proceedings.

Portugal.answer: Portugal's food and veterinary authority DGAV says that on arrival from a non-EU country you cannot bring meat, milk or their products, except up to 10 kg from the Faroe Islands or Greenland. You may bring up to 2 kg in total of infant milk, infant food, medical special foods and medically needed pet feed, up to 20 kg of fish and some shellfish, and up to 2 kg of other animal products such as honey, live oysters, live mussels and snails. Products that do not comply must be declared to Customs; undeclared ones are seized and destroyed, and the sheet says you may face further consequences. The DGAV data sheet we read was reviewed in May 2021.
sources: https://www.dgav.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Viajar-com-produtos-de-origem-animal-EN.pdf
DGAV (Portugal) — Data sheet: travelling with products of animal origin from non-EU countries (reviewed May 2021)
faq: Can I bring meat or milk products into Portugal from outside the EU?
No, except from the Faroe Islands or Greenland, up to 10 kg per person. The DGAV sheet shows meat and milk products as items you cannot bring.
What can I bring for a baby or for health reasons?

Powdered infant milk, infant food, special foods needed for medical reasons and special pet feed needed for medical reasons: 2 kg per person at most (10 kg from the Faroe Islands or Greenland), if it needs no refrigeration, is a proprietary brand and the packaging is unbroken.
How much fish can I bring?
Up to 20 kg per person, or the weight of one fish if that is more; the sheet lists fresh gutted, dried, cooked, cured or smoked fish and some crustaceans and shellfish.
What if I arrive with a product that breaks the rules?
Declare it to Customs at the EU airport or port. If Customs find it undeclared, it is seized and destroyed, and the sheet says you may also face further consequences.

Peru.answer: Peru's agriculture health service SENASA lets travellers bring a short list of dried or processed plant products up to 1 kg, and, for animal products, packaged and labelled pasteurised dairy up to 5 kg (or one cheese up to 10 kg), sausages other than pork up to 10 kg, canned fast food other than pork up to 2 kg, and honey, royal jelly or pollen up to 1 kg. Fresh fruit, flowers, plants, wood and live insects need SENASA's prior authorisation, soil is not allowed, and pork products are banned because of African swine fever. Everything must be declared, and food from the aeroplane must not be taken off the flight.
sources: https://www.gob.pe/institucion/senasa/campa%C3%B1as/6969-amigo-viajero
SENASA (Peru) — Amigo viajero: plant and animal products allowed as accompanied baggage (last changed 10 May 2024)
faq: Can I bring fruit into Peru?

Fresh or naturally dried fruit and flowers, wood, live insects, plants or parts of plants need SENASA's prior authorisation and cannot come in baggage without the plant-health checks. Only industrially dried fruit and vegetables are on the list of items allowed up to 1 kg.
Can I bring cheese, sausages or honey?

Packaged and labelled, from a country without health restrictions: pasteurised dairy up to 5 kg or one cheese up to 10 kg, sausages (not pork) up to 10 kg, canned fast food (not pork) up to 2 kg, and honey, royal jelly or pollen up to 1 kg.
Can I bring pork products?
No. SENASA banned pork products from entering Peru to keep the country free of African swine fever.
What do I do with the food from my flight?
Eat it on the flight. If you take it off the aeroplane, the SENASA inspector confiscates it.

Mexico.answer: Mexico's agriculture department (SADER, with SENASICA) says you must declare any agri-food product in your luggage on arrival; an officer then assesses its sanitary condition and decides whether it can enter, must be returned, or is destroyed. The page lists as restricted: soil and plant material, artisanal hams, sausages and cheeses, animal-origin flours, dairy, and fresh, dried, canned or frozen poultry, pork, beef and fish, plus shellfish and crustaceans. The page we read is from July 2017 and gives no quantity limits.
sources: https://www.gob.mx/agricultura/articulos/que-alimentos-puedo-movilizar-dentro-y-fuera-de-mexico
SADER (Mexico) — What products can I bring into Mexico? (12 July 2017)
faq: Do I have to declare food when I arrive in Mexico?

Yes. SADER says that if you declare agri-food products in your luggage, an officer from SENASICA evaluates their sanitary condition. Luggage on all flights can also be inspected for safety and pest control.
What decides whether my food can enter?
The SENASICA officer evaluates the declared product and decides whether a procedure applies, whether it is returned, or whether it is officially destroyed.
Which foods are restricted?

Artisanal hams, sausages and cheeses, animal-origin flours, dairy products, and fresh, dried, canned or frozen poultry, pork, beef and fish, plus shellfish and crustaceans. Soil and plant material are restricted too.
Why are these products restricted?
The page says they could bring pests and diseases that are not present in the country.

South Africa.answer: The South African government says you must have a permit from the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development for items such as meat, dairy, honey, eggs, live animals, fresh produce, seeds or wood, and these may also need a health certificate from the country they come from. Goods that need a permit must be declared to customs on arrival; failing to declare them can lead to confiscation or fines. The gov.za page gives no quantity limits and shows no update date.
sources: https://www.gov.za/faq/travel-tourism/what-goods-may-i-bring-south-africa

faq: Can I bring meat, dairy or eggs into South Africa?
You need a permit from the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development for meat, dairy, honey and eggs, and a health certificate from the country of origin may also be required.
Can I bring fruit, vegetables or seeds?
The page lists fresh produce, seeds and wood among the items that need a Department of Agriculture permit.
Do I have to declare these goods?
Yes. Goods that need a permit must be declared to customs on arrival. If you are unsure, the page says it is safest to declare them.

Brazil.answer: Brazil's agriculture ministry (MAPA) tells travellers who are unsure how an item is classified to declare it and present themselves to the Vigiagro agricultural inspectors through the customs channel 'Bens a Declarar'. Travellers who visited agricultural production or exhibition areas in the last 15 days must also declare this. Your bag may be selected for agricultural inspection, Vigiagro decides whether goods may enter, and non-compliant items can be destroyed. The MAPA page we read (updated 24 September 2026) lists the categories but gives no per-item verdicts or quantity limits in the part we read.
sources: https://www.gov.br/agricultura/pt-br/assuntos/vigilancia-agropecuaria/viajantes-e-bagagens/lista-de-bens-agropecuarios-que-podem-ou-nao-ingressar-no-brasil
Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAPA, Brazil) — List of agricultural goods that may or may not enter Brazil in travellers' baggage (updated 24 September 2026)
faq: Do I have to declare food or plants when I arrive in Brazil?
MAPA advises you to declare any item you are unsure how to classify and to present yourself to Vigiagro through customs, using the 'Bens a Declarar' (goods to declare) channel.
Who decides whether my goods can enter?
Vigiagro, the agricultural inspection service. Your bag may be selected for federal agricultural inspection.
What if I visited a farm or agricultural fair before the trip?
If you were in agricultural production or exhibition areas in the last 15 days, you must declare it and present yourself to Vigiagro.
What happens to goods that do not meet the rules?
The page says non-compliant items can lead to loss or destruction of the products and retention of animals.

Turkey.answer: The Turkish Ministry of Trade's customs guide lists the consumer food you may bring duty-free when you arrive: 1 kg each of tea, instant coffee, coffee, chocolate and sugar-based sweets, together with the tobacco, alcohol and cosmetics allowances. The goods must accompany the passenger. The page we read has a revision date of 4 December 2018 and does not cover meat, dairy, fruit, plants or any ban, so ask Turkish customs or the agriculture ministry before you bring them.

faq: How much tea, coffee or chocolate can I bring into Turkey?
The Ministry of Trade guide lists 1 kg each of tea, instant coffee, coffee, chocolate and sugar-based sweets as duty-free consumer goods, if they accompany you.
Is there an age limit?
Passengers under 18 cannot use the tobacco or alcohol exemptions; the page states no age limit for the food items.
Can I bring meat, cheese or fruit into Turkey?
The page we read does not cover them. Ask Turkish customs or the Ministry of Agriculture before you bring meat, dairy, fruit, vegetables or plants.
What happens if I bring more than the amounts?
The page does not say what happens above the limits, and it states that it is guidance that does not replace customs legislation.

Greece.answer: Flying into Greece from outside the EU, you follow the EU food rules: no meat or dairy, only small amounts of fruit, vegetables, eggs and honey, fish up to 20 kg and up to 2 kg of baby or medical food. Athens International Airport says Greek customs works on site, that you declare cash of €10,000 or more before leaving the baggage claim area, and it gives a customs email for questions. That airport page says nothing about food, so the food limits come from the EU page.

No. The EU page rules out meat and dairy for travellers from outside the EU, with one narrow exception for under 10 kg from the Faroe Islands or Greenland.
Where do I declare things at Athens airport?

Athens International Airport lists currency declaration offices in the baggage claim area, and says cash of €10,000 or more must be declared before you leave it. The airport page gives no separate food declaration point.
Who can I ask about Greek customs at the airport?
The airport page gives an email for Greek customs at Athens airport: tel.el-venizelos@aade.gr.
How much baby food or fish may I bring?
The EU page allows up to 2 kg of powdered infant milk, infant food or medical food in sealed retail packs, and fish up to 20 kg or one fish, whichever is heavier.

Lithuania.answer: Lithuanian Customs says that from a non-EU country you may bring up to 5 kg of fruit and vegetables for yourself, but potatoes are banned outright. Seeds, bulbs and flowers have small limits, and since June 2024 a Lithuanian ban covers agricultural products and food from Russia and Belarus. For meat and dairy the customs page points to the European Commission, whose rule is that they are not allowed.

faq: Can I bring potatoes into Lithuania?
No. Lithuanian Customs says importing potatoes from non-EU countries for private use is prohibited.
How much fruit and vegetables can I bring into Lithuania?
Up to 5 kg of vegetables and fruit for private use, according to Lithuanian Customs.
Can I bring food from Russia or Belarus?

No. A Lithuanian government resolution has banned imports of agricultural products and food originating in Russia or Belarus since 3 June 2024. Its list covers meat, fish, milk, eggs, honey, vegetables, fruit, sugar, sweets, drinks and more.

Denmark.answer: Borger.dk, the Danish public portal, says you may not take meat, meat products, milk or dairy home from outside the EU, nor composite products containing meat. Other animal products such as honey, eggs and snails, and long-life sweets, pasta and baked goods, are capped at 2 kg, fish at 20 kg, and fresh fruit, vegetables and berries need a plant health certificate. Flour and grain have no limit. The page shows no date.

faq: How much honey or eggs can I take back to Denmark?
Up to 2 kg of other animal products without meat or milk, such as honey, eggs and snails.
Can I bring biscuits, pasta or bread home?
Yes, long-life composite products without meat count toward the same 2 kg limit. The page names sweets, pasta and couscous, muesli and cereals, bread, cakes and biscuits.
Do I need a certificate for fruit and vegetables?

Fresh vegetables, berries and fruit need a plant health certificate from the country you leave, and getting it is your responsibility. Pineapple, banana, date, durian and coconut are listed as freely allowed.
How much fish can I bring from outside the EU?
Fish and fish products up to 20 kg, and a whole fish heavier than 20 kg is also allowed. Sturgeon caviar is limited to 125 g per person in marked, sealed containers.
Is the Faroe Islands or Greenland different?
Yes. From there you may take up to 10 kg of meat, dairy and other animal products, with no limit on fish, and fresh vegetables, fruit and berries may not be taken home.

Can I bring sweets and biscuits to Estonia from a third country?
Yes, in quantities for personal use, if they contain no milk or meat. The page gives candy, chocolate, biscuits and cakes as examples.
How much fish and caviar can I bring?
Up to 20 kg of gutted fresh fish per person, but not black caviar. Each traveller may bring 125 g of sturgeon caviar without a CITES permit, if the packaging is marked.
What about spices, rice and nuts?
EMTA says some foods from certain countries are under temporary stricter control with border veterinary checks. Fresh goods under 5 kg and dried goods under 2 kg are exempt.
Is there an extra charge on goods from Russia or Belarus?
Yes. From 20 July 2025 an additional 50% customs duty applies to listed goods such as meat, milk, honey, fruit and vegetables.

topics.head: Bulgaria follows the EU ban on meat and dairy from outside the EU.

scen.when: Salami, ham, cheese, yoghurt from a non-EU country
lines: The EU page forbids meat and dairy for travellers from outside the EU.
Undeclared items are confiscated and destroyed, with a possible fine or prosecution.

scen.when: From the Faroe Islands or Greenland
lines: 10 kg each of meat, dairy, honey and eggs.

topics.label: Fruit, plants & honey
topics.head: Small personal amounts of produce; plants need a certificate.

lines: No figure is given for fruit, vegetables or eggs; products like honey up to 2 kg.
A phytosanitary certificate is required.

topics.label: Fish
topics.head: Fish up to 20 kg, or one fish if heavier.

scen.when: Fresh gutted, prepared or processed fish
lines: Take the larger of 20 kg or a single fish.

topics.label: Baby & medical food
topics.head: Baby milk, baby food and medical food up to 2 kg.

scen.when: Powdered infant milk, baby food, medical food
lines: Shelf-stable, branded retail packs, unbroken unless in use.

scen.when: Pet food needed for health reasons
lines: For the pet travelling with you, sealed retail pack.

topics.label: Not covered
topics.head: No Bulgarian national page was readable.

lines: Bulgarian Customs Agency and Food Safety Agency pages did not open, so any Bulgarian detail is missing.
Ask Bulgarian customs before you bring anything not listed.
